conditional_states.detail: packages/web `vite build` (v8/rolldown native bundler, 8303 modules) is OOM-killed at ~3.1GB RSS in the 4GB sandbox (dmesg oom-kill evidence). Upstream's Docker E2E gate runs the same build on GitHub-hosted 7GB runners. The documented dev-mode launch (pnpm dev:web) does not require the production renderer bundle and is what was verified.

Desktop Electron main process, zcode-host utility process, agent warmup, database-startup and CDP were verified running under Xvfb. The dev-mode renderer (unbundled vite module graph of @zcode/ui) loaded (vite connected, preload bridge window.zcode present, database-startup relay active) but the renderer process crashed (render-process-gone) under the sandbox's memory ceiling while loading the full module graph.

Upstream's WDIO desktop e2e (container-boot, smoke, e2ecase-regression, upstream-provider, task-list-archive-confirmation — the Docker gate set) starts in this sandbox (Xvfb + chromedriver preflight) but its onPrepare step performs the same desktop production build that exceeds the 4GB sandbox. Recorded as an explicit environment limitation, not a product failure.

In web-only dev mode (pnpm dev:web), submitting a task from the browser UI fails with project.remote-project-required: the web client routes project/session creation through the remote-host policy (web dev mode has no local desktop host; upstream README documents ZCODE_SERVER_WORKSPACE for dev:web source development). The supported full-chain task flows — the Electron desktop and the Agent CLI — were verified instead, with the CLI delivering complete real-task evidence.

The supplied OpenRouter key holds ~10 token credits (billing_error on paid models: 'can only afford 9') and Anthropic-backed models are geo-restricted from this sandbox's egress region (permission_error 'not available in your region'). Worked around by binding the OpenRouter provider to the free-tier model nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b:free (openai-chat-completions endpoint), which executed the real tasks. Anthropic-format and chat-completions endpoints were both proven reachable with real HTTP exchanges.
No Next.js status console was used as evidence; every item above comes from the original ZCode application (web UI at :5173/:3030, Electron desktop under Xvfb, and apps/zcode-cli agent runtime).
